flashcard_questions.q: What does the term sanctity of life mean?
flashcard_questions.a: The belief that all human life is sacred because God created it.

flashcard_questions.q: What does quality of life mean in the euthanasia debate?
flashcard_questions.a: Whether a person’s life is worth living, judged by comfort and freedom from pain.

flashcard_questions.q: What is ensoulment in Islamic teaching?
flashcard_questions.a: The moment the soul enters the foetus, traditionally held to be 120 days into pregnancy.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the Arabic term haram mean?
What is the principle of double effect?
flashcard_questions.a: An action with a good intended outcome is acceptable even if it has an unintended harmful consequence.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the Catholic Church’s teaching on abortion?
flashcard_questions.a: It is always wrong, because life begins at conception and is sacred.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the Church of England’s position on abortion?
flashcard_questions.a: Generally opposed, but it may be accepted when the mother’s life is at risk.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Bible verse do Christians cite to show humans are made in God’s image?
Which Qur’an verse warns against killing children for fear of poverty?
What words complete Job 1:21: “The Lord gave and the Lord has ____ ____”?
Why do Christians and Muslims support palliative care while opposing euthanasia?
flashcard_questions.a: It relieves suffering without deliberately hastening death.

flashcard_questions.q: What is Yawm al-Din in Islam?
flashcard_questions.a: The Day of Judgement, when Allah resurrects everyone and judges their deeds.

flashcard_questions.q: What do humanists argue should guide moral decisions about dying?
flashcard_questions.a: Reducing suffering in this life, since they do not believe in an afterlife.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does belief in an afterlife strengthen religious opposition to euthanasia?
flashcard_questions.a: Cutting short a life that prepares for eternity may carry spiritual consequences.

notes: 14 cards: 5 term→definition (sanctity/quality of life, ensoulment, haram, palliative care), 2 denomination→position (Catholic, Church of England), 2 belief→source (Genesis 1:27, Qur’an 17:31), 1 cloze on Job 1:21, 2 argument→view (humanist, afterlife), 2 practice/effect cards. Dropped 'afterlife' and 'abortion' as glossary flavour — both are covered more precisely by other cards.
